title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD1RF_1RE0RB_1LA0RD_0RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD1RF_1RE0RB_1LA0RD_0RE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a row of blocks (10)n separated by S = 01100, with one defect (a single 0 or 1 in place of an S). Every time the head reaches a new cell at the right end (an E-record) one sweep has run left to the defect and back. Lean proves (kernel) the four generic sweep rules, for every block size and every tape left of the defect, and that the run from blank tape reaches such a record. A Python macro simulator built from symbolic one-sweep runs, checked tape for tape against direct simulation, runs 5.69·106 sweeps (2.96·1013 steps) without a halt. With native_decide: no halt in the first 107 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: The cell gadgets
claims.text: The leftward signal crosses a block (10)^n A>1 in 2n steps (across) and a separator S in 21 steps, leaving (10)^2 1 on its right (sgad); it turns at a defect 1 (2Y + 4 steps, turn1) or at a defect 0 after a block of at least 2 (2Y + 16 steps, turn0); D, going right, turns each (10)^(w+2) 1 into S (10)^w (2w + 5 steps, dunit). Written by bbtools.symtm.prove, for all sizes and all surrounding tapes.

claims.title: The generic sweep rules
claims.text: For an E-record T d y S w1 S … S wr S z 1 E>0, any r, any tape T: defect 1 becomes 0, y + 3, z − 2 (record_d1, 4z + 4y + 40 + Σ(4w + 26) steps, rcost_eq); defect 0 after a block x + 2: x − 2, defect 1, y + 5, z − 2 (record_d0, 12 steps more); the same for a zone of one block (record1_d1: z + 1; record1_d0: x − 2, z + 3). Each sweep passes over the whole zone and lengthens the tape by two cells.

claims.title: The run reaches the rules
claims.text: From blank tape the machine is at the E-record 2 S 2 S 2 S 1 5 1 E>0 after 431 steps (list simulator, kernel evaluation), and by record1_d1 at 2 S 2 S 2 S 0 6 1 E>0 after 457.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The macro simulator agrees with the machine
claims.text: py/mac15b.py takes each sweep from a symbolic run (bbtools.symtm) on a window around the defect and the zone, with the middle of the zone abstracted and paid by the generic cost; all 891 window rules met are cached. It reproduces the whole tape and the step count at every E-record of the first 2·108 steps (12,384 from its start record at step 3513) (py/cmpm.py against c/erec.c), and the sample records up to 4.09·109 steps (py/verify_e27k.py). The run-length version py/mac15c.py agrees on 12,014 of them (py/test15c.py). About 80% of the sweeps follow the four generic rules; the rest are events at the end of the zone, at the left edge or when the defect moves.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.96·10<sup>13</sup> steps
claims.text: The macro simulator ran 5,692,991 sweeps, 29,654,000,000,000 steps (2.9654·1013), without a halting window. At the end the tape has 244,161 blocks, the zone is the whole tape (one defect), and the last blocks are 1048574 S 1048574 S 491400 (1048574 = 410 − 2).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 88,351 cells have been visited and 43,124 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Why it does not halt soon
claims.text: The machine can only stop with D>1 0 1 1 on the tape, which within a sweep means a turn at the defect with the first right block Y ≤ 1. In a zone of two or more blocks Y = y + 2 ≥ 2, so the generic rules never halt; in a zone of one block Y = z, and in the runs z only comes back as 2 after an event and then grows. No reachable window rule halts. The block sizes settle into values 4k − 2 (2, 14, 62, 254, …), each made by the n → 4n + 6 growth of a block as the defect passes, so the tape behaves like a counter whose digits are blocks; nothing in it is seen to drift toward a halting turn.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would need a closed set of macro configurations covering the events (the end of the zone running out, the defect reaching a frozen separator or the left edge), with the generic rules already in Lean.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine keeps its tape as blocks (10)n glued by a separator 01100, with one flaw somewhere: a single 0 or 1 where a separator should be. Every time the tape grows by two cells a signal runs left to the flaw and back, rewriting each block it crosses. Lean proves those sweeps exactly; a simulator built from them ran 3·1013 steps without a halt.

facts.text: The generic sweeps, for every block size and every tape (Lean, kernel).
No halt in the exact macro simulator (5.69·10<sup>6</sup> sweeps).
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494).
After 109 steps the tape spans 88,351 cells (6,365 left of the start, 50,204 right), with a density of 1s of 0.488.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Blocks, separators and one defect
html: Look at the tape each time the head is in state E on a new cell at the right end, with a 1 just left of it: an E-record. It is always made of blocks (10)n (write <n>), each followed by a separator: usually S = 01100, but at one place (sometimes a few) a single 0 or 1. The last of those is the defect; the blocks right of it, all separated by S, form the zone.

The record at step 431: <2> S <2> S <2> S 1 <5> 1 E>0, a defect 1 and a zone of one block. At step 2·108: about 1,970 blocks <2>, then 137 blocks <14>, then <62> <303> <853> <2150> <1118>, all separated by S.

sections.heading: One sweep: left to the defect and back
html: From an E-record the head writes a 1 and a signal (state A on a 1) runs left. Crossing a block <n> costs 2n steps and shifts the block one cell; crossing a separator S costs 21 steps and leaves (10)2 1 behind: every block right of an S is carried back as a block two larger. At the defect the signal turns:

• defect 1: it becomes 0 and the first zone block y grows by 3;
  • defect 0 after a block x ≥ 2: x loses 2, the defect becomes 1, y grows by 5.

Then D runs right, turning each (10)w+2 1 back into S <w>, and at the blank end writes the 1 of the next E-record. Net effect: the last block z pays 2, the tape is 2 cells longer. In Lean these are record_d1 and record_d0, for zones of any length, cost 4z + 4y + 40 + Σ(4w + 26) steps.

sections.heading: Events and a counter of blocks 4<sup>k</sup> − 2
html: The generic rules alternate the defect between 1 and 0, feed the first zone block (+3, +5) and drain the last (−2), and eat the block before the defect 2 at a time. When something runs out an event happens: the last block reaching 0 or 1 makes the S before it the new defect and freezes the old one; a block before a 0-defect below 2 merges blocks and moves the defect left; at the left edge two-blocks <2> S are added. About one sweep in five is an event.

Over long runs the blocks settle on the values 2, 14, 62, 254, 1022, …, 4k − 2: a block grows n → 4n + 6 as the defect passes it. The tape is a counter whose digits are runs of equal blocks, read from the right, while the left edge grows in bursts of <2> blocks. After 2.96·1013 steps there are 244,161 blocks and the right end reads … S <1048574> S <1048574> S <491400>.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1, reached from D>1 0 1 1. Inside a sweep this is a turn at the defect where the block just right of it is 0 or 1 on the way back. In a zone of two or more blocks that block is y + 2 ≥ 2, so the generic rules cannot halt; in a zone of one block it is z, which in the runs only returns as 2 after an event and then grows. None of the 891 window rules the simulator met halts.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel (lean/Gadgets.lean, lean/Macro.lean): the cell gadgets; the leftward and rightward passes over a zone of any length (apass, dpass); the four generic sweep rules with exact step counts; the run from blank tape reaching the record at step 431 and following record1_d1 to step 457.
Lean, native_decide (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in the first 107 steps.

Computed: the macro simulator (symbolic window rules) checked tape for tape against the machine at every E-record of the first 2·108 steps and at samples to 4·109; then run to 2.96·1013 steps with no halt.
Open: the events are not in Lean, and no closed set of configurations excluding a halting turn is known.

family: signal sweeps over S-separated (10)^n blocks with one moving defect; counter-like blocks 4^k-2
summary: The tape is blocks (10)<sup>n</sup> separated by 01100 with one moving defect; a signal sweeps left to the defect and back each time the tape grows by two cells, and Lean proves the generic sweep rules; no halt in 3·10<sup>13</sup> steps of an exact macro simulator.
